### 0. Your Sheet (sets itself up)
Looks for a Google Sheet called `sheetName` in your Drive. On the first run it isn't there, so the workflow creates it with **4 tabs** and header rows:
- **Searches**: your list (input, with 4 example rows): role, city, country (2 letters), `active` = no skips a row.
- **History**: one row per role x city x week (the data; a rerun of the same week overwrites that week's row).
- **Summary**: one row per role x city with the latest week, the week before, the change and a trend; ready for a chart.
- **Runs**: a log of every Apify run.
Later runs find the Sheet by name. Rename it in Drive? Change `sheetName` too.

parameters.content:
### Long runs: nothing waits for hours
Apify runs are **started without waiting** and logged in the **Runs** tab of your Sheet (started_at, search, mode, status, jobs, charged_usd, run_url, collected_at, note).

1. **Collect first:** runs still marked RUNNING from an earlier execution are checked. A finished run is read and processed, then marked SUCCEEDED with `collected_at`: a run is never processed twice. FAILED, ABORTED or TIMED-OUT runs get that status and a note.
2. **Start:** new runs for this execution all start at once. A search whose previous run is still RUNNING is not started again (no double cost).
3. **Wait:** every 70 seconds the runs are checked, for at most `maxWaitMinutes` (default 30). A run that is not finished by then stays RUNNING and is collected by the next scheduled execution or manual run.

Waits longer than 65 seconds are stored in n8n's database, so an n8n restart does not lose a run: it is still in the Runs tab.

**Keep your schedule shorter than your Apify data retention.** A run's results live in an unnamed dataset. Apify keeps unnamed storages according to your plan: on the Free plan your 10 most recent runs are kept for 4 months, on paid plans the period is set in your billing settings (docs.apify.com/platform/storage/usage). Run the workflow more often than that.

**Where to see every run:** the **Runs** tab (open `run_url`), Apify Console > Runs, and n8n > Executions.

**About `charged_usd`:** it is what the run itself charged (pay-per-event price x events). job-feed starts its own sub-runs (one per job board / company reader); those are billed as separate runs and show up in Apify Console > Runs. The full total is in Apify Console > Billing.

**Faster than waiting:** set `webhookUrl` (see the webhook note). Without it, scheduled collection still works.

### Faster results with a webhook (optional)
Apify can call this workflow the moment a run finishes. The **Apify run finished** node is a second trigger for that.
- **n8n Cloud:** open the **Apify run finished** node, copy its **Production URL**, paste it into `webhookUrl` in Settings, and **activate** the workflow.
- **Self-hosted:** needs a public HTTPS URL (Cloudflare Tunnel or a reverse proxy; set n8n's `WEBHOOK_URL`). localhost alone cannot receive Apify webhooks.
- Leave `webhookUrl` empty to skip this: every run is still collected by the schedule (and the workflow then waits up to `maxWaitMinutes` for runs it started).

With `webhookUrl` set, the workflow does not wait: it starts the runs and ends. The webhook (or the next schedule) collects each result once. A webhook for a run that is not in the Runs tab is ignored.

### Runs tab
One row per Apify run. Open `run_url` for the run in Apify Console. The workflow reads this tab to collect runs that were still running last time and never processes a run twice. `charged_usd` is what that run itself charged. The full total is in Apify Console > Billing.

parameters.content:
## Weekly job market report: how many job ads per role and city, in Google Sheets
Every Monday this workflow counts the new job ads of the last 7 days for each role and city on your list, from many job boards at once, and stores the numbers in a Google Sheet: a **History** tab (one row per role, city and week) and a **Summary** tab (latest week, the week before, change and trend) that is ready for a chart. Use it for job market data without a subscription: recruiters and sourcers (where is hiring growing?), HR and salary teams, career coaches, bootcamps and analysts. It reads public job ads only and sends nothing.

**How it works**
1. Finds (or on the first run creates) your Sheet with 4 tabs: **Searches** (your list, 4 examples), **History**, **Summary**, **Runs**.
2. Reads the active rows of **Searches**: `role`, `city`, `country` (2 letters). Searches already stored for this week are skipped; at most `maxSearchesPerRun` (4) start per run.
3. The Apify actor `santamaria-automations/job-feed` runs one search per row: the role as keyword, the city and country, ads posted in the last `postedWithinDays` (7) days, at most `maxAdsPerSearch` (30) unique ads, titles filtered by `minRelevanceScore` (50). Runs start **without waiting** and are logged in the **Runs** tab (see the sticky "Long runs"). Optional: a webhook delivers results the moment a run finishes.
4. For each run the workflow reads how many unique ads job-feed delivered (the dataset item count; no rows are downloaded).
5. **History** gets a row per role x city x week (`ads`, `capped`, `cap`, `run_url`); **Summary** gets one row per role x city with `previous_week`, `previous_ads`, `change`, `change_pct` and `trend` (first week, up, down, same, capped).

**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Install the verified community node `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` (install guide: https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/n8n). You need an Apify account (free to start: https://console.apify.com/sign-up?fpr=0khfbz). Connect it in **Get job market run status** and **Count the job ads of each run**, and in **Start job market run (no waiting)** (credential type Apify API).
2. Connect Google Sheets (Sheet nodes and the HTTP nodes that set it up).
3. Run once with **Test workflow**: the Sheet is created with 4 example searches. Open the **Searches** tab and replace them with your roles and cities (country = 2 letters).
4. Run again or wait for Monday, then activate. Times use your n8n timezone.

**Cost** (at Apify Store prices, checked 2026-11-23, from the job-feed README rate card and examples): job-feed bills $0.0005 per unique job, and the job boards it reads bill on top; the README budgets about $0.40-$0.80 per 100 jobs without detail fetch. Default config: 4 searches x up to 30 ads = up to 120 ads per week = about $0.48-$0.96 per week (about $2-$4 per month). More roles or cities, a higher `maxAdsPerSearch` or a daily schedule raise it in proportion. `maxCostPerRunUsd` (0.25 per run) is a budget setting, not a guaranteed hard stop. n8n and Google Sheets as per your plans.

**Limits**
- The count is capped by `maxAdsPerSearch` to keep the cost small. `capped` = yes means "at least this many ads"; raise the cap for big cities or broad roles, and the cost grows with it.
- It counts unique job ads that job-feed found on the boards it supports (see https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/job-feed) in the city radius `radiusKm` (25 km): a sample of the market, not a census, and coverage differs by country.
- The same job on several boards is counted once; jobs posted under a different title may be missed or filtered by `minRelevanceScore`.
- Weeks start on Monday in your n8n timezone. Re-running the same week overwrites that week's History row only when `reRunSameWeek` is true; otherwise finished searches are skipped.
- Use the numbers as a trend indicator.

### Settings explained
- `maxSearchesPerRun` (4): job-feed runs started per execution; the other rows of Searches follow in the next execution (searches stored for this week are skipped), which also keeps cost bounded.
- `maxAdsPerSearch` (30): unique ads per search. Cost = ads x about $0.004-$0.008 (README range). `capped` = yes in the Sheet means the real number is higher.
- `postedWithinDays` (7): the window. Seven days with a weekly schedule = new ads of that week.
- `radiusKm` (25): around the city. `minRelevanceScore` (50): drops ads whose title shares less than half of the role words.
- `includeGlobalBoards` (true): also Indeed, Glassdoor and LinkedIn for the country; false is cheaper and narrower.
- `reRunSameWeek` (false): true overwrites this week's rows.
- `sheetName`: your Google Sheet. `maxWaitMinutes` (15), `apifyRunTimeoutMinutes` (30), `maxCostPerRunUsd` (0.25), `webhookUrl` (empty = off).

### Searches tab (your list)
One row per role and city. `role` is used as the search keyword (use the words in the job title: "Data Analyst", "Pflegefachperson"), `city` as the location, `country` as a 2-letter code (DE, CH, AT, US, GB ...), `active` = no skips a row. An empty tab stops the workflow with a message before any Apify cost.

### History and Summary (chart-ready)
**History**: one row per week, role and city (`ads`, `capped`). Select the columns week, role, city, ads and use Insert > Chart (or a pivot table: rows = week, columns = role, values = ads) for a trend line.
**Summary**: one row per role and city with the latest week, `previous_ads`, `change`, `change_pct` and `trend`. Select role, city, ads and insert a column chart for the ranking.
The workflow only writes its own columns; add your own to the right.

### If something goes wrong
- **"No active search ..."** or **"country must be 2 letters"**: fix the Searches tab. No Apify cost has been spent.
- **A run fails** (timeout): the Runs tab shows the status and a note; that search is tried again next time (no History row exists for it).
- **ads = 0**: no matching ads in the window; check spelling, city and country, or widen `postedWithinDays`.
